# Synthetic student CSV import corpus

All data is synthetic and generated. Names, emails and phones are invented.
Email addresses use only `example.com`, `example.net`, `example.org` and
`example.invalid`. Every phone number uses the 555 exchange. Valid dates are
between 1950 and 2026. Street and city names are invented too.

The 12 dialects use neutral vocabularies. They are not any vendor's actual
export format. This corpus proves parser behaviour and specifies matcher
behaviour only. It is not evidence that any real migration works. Until the
production matcher exists, its assertions skip with
`duplicate matcher not present yet`; parser, mapper and planner checks still run.

## Generate and test

From the repository root, using Python 3.11:

```sh
python3 -I backend/tests/fixtures/csv_import/corpus/generate_corpus.py --out backend/tests/fixtures/csv_import/corpus
```

The generator imports only the standard library. `scenarios.json` contains the
scenario templates, seeds, dialect column sources and compact outcome snapshots
captured from the real parser, mapper and planner. Snapshots retain mappings,
validity, error codes and notes, without planner `data` dictionaries. Dates and
legal names come from authored source facts alongside the display templates;
these include the finite missing-name cases in the grid. The generator derives
all expected mapped data and identity labels from those facts. The harness
still checks every field of every live planned data dictionary against that
expected data. There is no general replacement CSV parser or planner. No
network, database or credentials are needed.

`--out` writes `manifest.json` or `manifest.json.gz` and the materialised `files/`
subset. Both JSON documents use sparse row expectations before compression.
Documents above 1,000,000 bytes after compaction use gzip; smaller documents stay
plain JSON. The generator and harness read either form transparently. The
combined committed document size must stay at most 2,000,000 bytes. Gzip headers
have a zero timestamp and no filename, so compressed outputs are deterministic.

For review, write readable plain JSON without changing the committed files:

```sh
python3 -I backend/tests/fixtures/csv_import/corpus/generate_corpus.py --expand /tmp/koaryu-manifest-expanded.json
python3 -I backend/tests/fixtures/csv_import/corpus/generate_corpus.py --document scenarios --expand /tmp/koaryu-scenarios-expanded.json
```

The manifest expansion restores every omitted row. The scenario expansion
renders the compact catalogue as readable JSON.

Files larger than 1 MiB have `materialized: false` and are absent from Git. To regenerate one
file, including one above that threshold:

```sh
python3 -I backend/tests/fixtures/csv_import/corpus/generate_corpus.py --out /tmp/koaryu-corpus-one --only limit_rows_10000
```

That command writes only `files/limit_rows_10000.csv`, without changing a
manifest. UTF-16 output always uses a little-endian BOM. CSV line endings and
encodings are explicit, independent of the host's defaults. Output paths and
timestamps do not enter the manifest or the generated bytes.

From `backend/`:

```sh
venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_student_import_corpus.py -q
KOARYU_CORPUS_FULL=1 venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_student_import_corpus.py -q
venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_student_import_csv.py -q
venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check .
venv/bin/python -m ruff check tests/test_student_import_corpus.py tests/fixtures/csv_import/corpus/generate_corpus.py
```

The default run omits the three largest regenerated cases: 10,000 rows,
10,001 rows and the over-10-MiB rejection. The 9,999-row case regenerates and
runs by default. Setting `KOARYU_CORPUS_FULL=1` also runs the three omitted
cases. Their skips are independent of the matcher-only skips.

To intentionally update pipeline snapshots after reviewing a production change,
run this authoring command from `backend/`, then regenerate and review both JSON
files. Ordinary generation and tests never update these expectations.

```sh
venv/bin/python tests/test_student_import_corpus.py --capture-oracle
```

The authoring command disables `.env` loading and uses `StudentService(None)`,
`validate_csv_import_mapping`, `StudentImportPlanner(None)` and default
`CsvImportOptions()` with `studio_id=None`. Programs and belts remain unresolved
raw values. It examines every planned row, since `CsvImportResult.rows` contains
only rows with issues, and stores only non-default outcome metadata. Expected mapped
values come from the fixture templates, rather than stored planner output.

For a byte-for-byte regeneration comparison from the repository root:

```sh
corpus_a=$(mktemp -d /tmp/koaryu-corpus-a.XXXXXX)
corpus_b=$(mktemp -d /tmp/koaryu-corpus-b.XXXXXX)
python3 -I backend/tests/fixtures/csv_import/corpus/generate_corpus.py --out "$corpus_a"
python3 -I backend/tests/fixtures/csv_import/corpus/generate_corpus.py --out "$corpus_b"
diff -rq "$corpus_a" "$corpus_b"
```

## Coverage

There are 546 logical CSV files, of which 542 are materialised. Most contain
5 to 60 rows. Twenty medium files have 200 to 1,000 rows. Six have 2,000 to
9,999 rows. Exactly one has 10,000 rows, one has 10,001 rows and one exceeds
10 MiB. The committed CSV payload stays below 8 MB.

| Scenario family | Files |
| --- | ---: |
| `dialect_grid` | 250 |
| `reupload_pair` | 100 |
| `family_identity` | 96 |
| `family_scripts` | 10 |
| `size_medium` | 20 |
| `framing` | 17 |
| `size_boundary` | 9 |
| `identity_controls` | 6 |
| `mapping_reproduction` | 2 |
| `source_identity` | 36 |

| Dialect | Files |
| --- | ---: |
| `dialect_01_member_id_style` | 129 |
| `dialect_02_given_family` | 60 |
| `dialect_03_last_first` | 58 |
| `dialect_04_full_student` | 56 |
| `dialect_05_decorated` | 59 |
| `dialect_06_child_surname` | 58 |
| `dialect_07_guardian_parts` | 22 |
| `dialect_08_duplicate_email` | 22 |
| `dialect_09_attendance` | 21 |
| `dialect_10_billing_nickname` | 21 |
| `dialect_11_address_middle` | 20 |
| `dialect_12_semicolon` | 20 |

The `source_identity` family has six files each for corrected legal names with the
same ID, repeated IDs in one file, IDs absent from the roster, IDs on some rows,
all eight candidate ID columns in reverse priority order, and IDs over 120
characters. It covers every alias and UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM and UTF-16. Over-long
cases also prove the 120-character boundary and trimming.

Source-ID mapping selects one column, independent of column order, in this
priority: Student ID, Member ID, Member #, Member Number, Legacy Account #,
Account #, Account Number, ID. Other candidates stay unmapped. The mapped ID is
trimmed and saved with source system `csv`. Empty IDs stay absent. Other mapping
rules, including duplicate-target rejections, are unchanged.

The grid varies names, middle names, quoted nicknames, preferred names, particles,
suffixes, dates, status aliases, invalid statuses, program/belt references,
encodings and framing. Date cases include ISO, US slashes, two-digit years,
dotted dates, English month names, Excel serials, ISO datetimes, blanks, year-only
values, invalid months and a birth date after the fixed business date.
Two-digit years represent 2000 through 2025 to avoid the platform's century
pivot introducing birthdays outside the allowed range.

Framing cases include BOM and plain UTF-8, cp1252 with curly quotes and accents,
UTF-16 BOM, CRLF and LF, embedded newlines and quotes, blank records, trailing
commas, short rows, extra cells, malformed quotes, duplicate headers, missing
header names, header-only and empty files. Column and cell cases include exactly
100 columns, 101 physical columns and exactly 32,000 characters in a cell. The
101-column case repeats a skipped header, so its auto-mapping has 100 dictionary
keys and validates. The parser rejects the physical column count before its
duplicate-header check.

The 16 family variants each have six versions. They cover twins, three siblings,
step-siblings, Sr/Jr parent and child, unrelated namesakes, missing birth dates,
repeated names with punctuation changes, changed emails, archived students,
sibling emails, conflicting birthdays, guardian spelling changes, different
parents sharing an email, guardians without email, reused placeholders and an
invented staff contact for unrelated students. Explicit pre-existing rosters
accompany the cases that need them. Controls also cover missing-date phone/name
matches, archived possible matches, existing guardian links and preferred names
that must not affect identity.

Each of the 51 re-upload pairs has a first upload A and an edited B. Fifty
belong to `reupload_pair`; the added CJK pair belongs to `family_scripts`. B corrects
six rows, removes three, adds two and reformats six others. B's existing roster
is the valid planned A rows, with stable `s<row_number>` student keys and one
`g<row_number>` guardian per imported row when a guardian name was mapped.
The harness verifies that roster against A's live planner results. Every B row
has identity labels against that roster.

The `family_scripts` files use invented test names in CJK, Cyrillic, Greek and
Arabic, plus mixed-script and transliterated spellings. They span five header
dialects and use UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM or UTF-16 with BOM. All dates and contact
values follow the same synthetic restrictions as the rest of the corpus.

| File id | Primary expected behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts_cjk_in_file` | Row 3 is `in_file_strong` against row 2; row 2's guardian is `new` |
| `scripts_cjk_existing` | Row 2 is `existing_strong`; its guardian is `link_existing` |
| `scripts_cyrillic_siblings` | Rows 2 and 3 are distinct students; their guardian is shared |
| `scripts_greek_parent_child` | Row 2 is `different_person`; its guardian is `separate_contact` |
| `scripts_arabic_diacritics` | Row 3 is `in_file_strong` after combining marks are dropped |
| `scripts_arabic_tatweel` | Row 3 is `none` because tatweel remains in row 2's name key |
| `scripts_mixed_repeat` | Row 3 is `in_file_strong` for the exact Latin/CJK repeat |
| `scripts_transliteration_limit` | Row 3 is `none` despite matching birth date, email and phone |
| `scripts_reupload_a` | First upload of 24 students with CJK names |
| `scripts_reupload_b` | Edited re-upload; 21 existing matches and 2 new students |

Arabic combining marks in `تَجْرِيبَا` disappear, giving the same key as `تجريبا`.
Tatweel, U+0640, in `تَـجْرِيبَا` is a modifier letter, not a combining mark.
NFKD preserves it and the Unicode word-token rule retains it. Those keys differ,
so `scripts_arabic_tatweel`, row 3, correctly has no match. No extra tatweel
removal rule is applied.

`测试曦 虚构` and `CeshiXi Xugou` in `scripts_transliteration_limit` represent the
same invented person. The supplied matching contract does not transliterate
names, so the different keys prevent a match. This is a known limit, even when
the date of birth and student contact details agree.

## Manifest schema

The root object has `version: 1`, `synthetic: true`,
`generator: "generate_corpus.py"`, `business_date_for_notes: "2026-10-21"` and a
`files` array. JSON is UTF-8; expectations are compact and may be gzip-compressed.
On-disk manifest `rows` arrays contain only exceptions to the defaults below.
The generator's `--expand` restores the full accepted manifest schema.
Each file entry has these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id`, `path` | Stable file id and relative `files/<id>.csv` path |
| `scenario`, `variant` | Scenario family and optional named variation |
| `dialect`, `seed` | Neutral vocabulary and deterministic generation seed |
| `encoding`, `line_ending` | Byte encoding and `lf` or `crlf` |
| `pair_of` | A's file id, present only on B |
| `row_count` | Logical nonblank data rows; 0 for empty/header-only files |
| `materialized` | Whether the CSV is committed, at most 1 MiB |
| `byte_count`, `sha256` | Exact generated size and content digest |
| `slow` | Whether this is one of the three largest regenerated files |
| `expected` | Pipeline expectations, existing roster and row labels |

In the expanded review document, `expected` contains:

```json
{
  "parse": "ok",
  "auto_mapping": {"Email": "email", "Student Email": "email"},
  "auto_mapping_valid": false,
  "mapping_rejection": "duplicate_target",
  "mapping": {"Email": "email", "Student Email": ""},
  "existing_roster": [],
  "rows": [
    {
      "row_number": 2,
      "valid": true,
      "error_codes": [],
      "duplicate": {"class": "none", "of_row": null, "of_existing": null, "reasons": []},
      "guardian": {"class": "none", "of_row": null, "of_existing": null, "reasons": []}
    }
  ]
}
```

The example shows the field shape; actual mappings list every header, including
skipped columns. For rejected files, mappings come from the raw header and
`rows` is empty. A rejecting parser returns no row count; `row_count` records
the constructed logical input count, and the harness verifies the rejection
instead of asserting a nonexistent parsed count.

`parse` is `ok` or `reject:<reason>`. Reasons are `empty`, `header_only`,
`duplicate_header`, `extra_cells`, `malformed_quote`, `too_many_rows`, `too_large`,
`too_many_columns` and `missing_header_name`.

The auto-mapping is the real mapper's unmodified result. When it fails mapping
validation, the manifest records `auto_mapping_valid: false` and
`mapping_rejection: "duplicate_target"`. The harness checks HTTP 400. The
corrected `mapping` keeps the first mapped occurrence of each target and skips
every later occurrence, walking headers in order. When the auto-mapping is
valid, `mapping` equals it. Row planning and identity labels use `mapping`.

An absent manifest row means `valid: true`, `error_codes: []`, no `notes`,
duplicate `class: "none"` and guardian `class: "new"` when the authored corrected
mapping supplies a guardian name, otherwise `"none"`. Both labels have null
`of_row` and `of_existing`, and empty `reasons`. Guardian presence comes from
scenario facts, not live planner output, so losing a mapped guardian still
fails verification. Every row with errors, notes or a non-default identity label
remains explicit. `in_file` and `existing` sub-objects appear only when both
sources apply.

The harness expands defaults by iterating every compacted row number from 2
through `row_count + 1`. It asserts validity, error codes, notes and expected
mapped data for every row, including those omitted from storage. When the
matcher exists it also asserts every expanded duplicate and guardian label.
Rejected files have no planned rows and retain an empty `rows` array.

Catalogue outcome rows are sparse too: absent metadata means valid with no
error codes or notes. No captured planner `data` dictionary is stored in the
catalogue; those dictionaries are reproduced from the source facts and checked
against every live plan. Re-upload rosters still preserve the full imported A
values, and the live-A roster check is unchanged.

`error_codes` includes only error-severity planner issues. Warning-severity
issues such as normalised statuses are not captured here; the existing CSV
import tests cover them. Row numbers are compacted after blank
records are removed: the first data record is 2, regardless of intervening blank
records. Future birthdays are not errors without a studio business date.
Instead those rows have
`"notes": ["future_date_of_birth_if_business_date"]`, relative to the fixed
business date above. A focused test supplies that date and proves the issue.

Existing students carry source system and ID when mapped, legal names, preferred name, ISO birth date or null,
email, phone, `archived`, `key` and a `guardians` array. Re-upload roster entries
also preserve all other mapped planner data. Guardians carry `key`,
`first_name`, `last_name`, email and phone.

`name_key` applies Unicode NFKD, removes combining marks, then casefolds. It
collects tokens with Python `re.findall(r"[^\W_]+", text)`, retaining letters and
digits from every script and discarding punctuation and underscores. A trailing
suffix token from `jr`, `sr`, `ii`, `iii`, `iv` is dropped, then the remaining
tokens are concatenated. Particles stay. Preferred names never establish
identity. Native-script names therefore retain non-empty keys; no
transliteration or tatweel removal is inferred.

Student labels use `none`, `in_file_strong`, `in_file_possible`,
`existing_strong`, `existing_possible`, `different_person` or `archived_match`.
They reference an earlier compacted row or an existing student key. Source-ID
strong matches take precedence over name strong matches, then possible matches
and different-person evidence. Source-ID candidates have reasons `["source_id"]`
and allow only Skip, including archived matches. Different or missing IDs leave
the name rules unchanged. Invalid rows never become student match targets.
Earlier rows win equal-confidence ties; the earliest row at that confidence is
used. When both sources match, `in_file` and `existing` sub-objects retain each
source's best evidence as well as the best overall fields. Archived matches
carry their underlying `strong` or `possible` confidence in `reasons`.
The specification gives no reason list for `different_person`; those labels
have an empty `reasons` array, without adding a reason convention to the contract.

Guardian labels use `none`, `new`, `link_existing`, `in_file_shared` or
`separate_contact`, with the same reference fields and ordered reasons. A
mapped guardian name is split on the first space. Guardian emails, phone numbers
and surnames never establish student identity. Preferred names do not establish
student identity either. No ambiguous guardian candidate precedence is needed
by the authored households: matching candidates satisfy the same rule or an
earlier numbered rule in the supplied specification.

## Current product gaps preserved by the fixtures

- `mapping_duplicate_email`, row 2, proves that `Email` plus `Student Email`
  auto-map to the same target and fail validation. The corrected mapping keeps
  `Email` and skips `Student Email`.
- `mapping_separate_guardian_names`, row 2, proves that separate guardian name
  headers both map to `guardian_name`. The corrected mapping keeps the first
  name only and skips the last-name column. The resulting guardian has an empty
  last name. Separate guardian first/last input is a documented unsupported shape.
- `grid_004`, row 2, proves that `Parent or Guardian` currently stays unmapped.
  Its populated source value therefore produces no planned guardian. This is a
  suspected missing header alias.
- `grid_012` proves that a semicolon-only file parses as one column. It does not
  receive delimiter detection, and required student fields can remain missing.
- `framing_utf8_plain`, row 8, records `Cancelled` as `invalid_status`. Current
  code recognises `Canceled`, with one L, rather than this spelling.

These observations describe behavior outside the source-ID amendment. They
remain covered by the fixtures.
